# Close location value - report

**Slug:** `family-close-location`
**Window:** 2016-01-04 -> 2023-12-29, development only. The 2024-2026
holdout was never loaded. A separate process deposited `holdout.json` / `holdout_run.log` in this folder after the development run; this agent did not read or use them.
**Execution:** `research/bt.py`, 1-minute marks, next-open fills, 2% band,
long-only, weights >= 0, sum <= 1. Headline 1 bp; 5 bp and 10 bp also reported.
**Primary:** CLV of the QQQ session (1-minute closes). If CLV < -0.80, hold
TQQQ for 5 sessions; otherwise BIL. A new event rolls the exit forward.

---

## 1. Headline

| cost | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | vol | TQQQ exposure | fills | turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **1 bp** | **79.32%** | **65.98%** | **1.37** | 1.95 | 53.3% | **45.8%** | 501 | 12,911x |
| 5 bp | 74.88% | 66.41% | 1.32 | 1.88 | 53.3% | 45.8% | 501 | 11,107x |
| 10 bp | 69.48% | 66.94% | 1.26 | 1.80 | 53.3% | 45.8% | 501 | 9,220x |

The stated bar is TQQQ **36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe**. The
local 1-minute benchmark is 36.15% / 82.29% / 0.80. The primary clears both at
1 bp, 5 bp and 10 bp.

Ending equity at 1 bp is **$10,594,516** from $100,000. The sleeve is in TQQQ
45.8% of bars and BIL 54.2%.

This is the strongest of the four new families, but it is also the most
volatile: a 66% drawdown, a -49.8% calendar year in 2022, and ~12,900x
turnover. The headline CAGR should be read with those three facts in view.

Daily-return correlation to TQQQ is **0.789**; correlation to the nine current
winners ranges from **0.425 to 0.789**.

## 2. Benchmarks

| | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | Calmar | TQQQ exposure |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| primary 1 bp | 79.32% | 65.98% | 1.37 | 1.20 | 45.8% |
| TQQQ | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 0.44 | 100% |
| QQQ | 18.91% | 37.30% | 0.90 | 0.51 | - |

## 3. Yearly returns and exposure

| year | strategy | TQQQ | TQQQ exposure | note |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 2016 | +65.0% | +19.9% | 39.7% | caught the February bottom and the post-election rally |
| 2017 | +39.7% | +114.5% | 25.1% | lags the calm bull |
| 2018 | **+47.5%** | -20.8% | 43.4% | the low-CLV bounce works in the Q4 bear |
| 2019 | +127.7% | +148.2% | 42.1% | close to TQQQ |
| 2020 | **+269.8%** | +104.1% | 52.6% | the crash-recovery payoff |
| 2021 | +105.5% | +81.1% | 44.8% | beats TQQQ |
| 2022 | **-49.8%** | -79.4% | 63.7% | loses less than TQQQ, still catastrophic |
| 2023 | **+257.1%** | +192.0% | 55.2% | beats TQQQ |

The profile is exactly what a dip-buying sleeve should look like: positive in
every development year, but with a -49.8% year in 2022 and a 66% peak-to-trough
drawdown. It beats TQQQ in 2016, 2018, 2020, 2021 and 2023 and lags in the calm
bull years 2017 and 2019. Unlike the Hurst and change-point families, it does
**not** depend on 2020: ex-2020 CAGR is 52.0%.

## 4. What the signal actually trades

226 event days, 125 closed episodes. The event-forward return is the TQQQ
open-to-open return over the 5 sessions after the signal.

| statistic | event-forward (5 sessions) | closed episodes |
|---|---:|---:|
| n | 226 | 125 |
| mean | **+2.92%** | +4.38% |
| median | +3.80% | +5.86% |
| win rate | 65.0% | 73.6% |
| t-stat | **4.31** | 4.60 |
| bootstrap p(mean <= 0) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| 95% CI | +1.60% .. +4.24% | +2.48% .. +6.19% |
| worst / best | -42.0% / +31.9% | -34.7% / +29.2% |

Both the event-level and the episode-level edges are strong and statistically
significant. The episode mean is larger than the event mean because the
position chains through overlapping CLV events and stays long through the
strongest runs. The worst event is -42.0% (a crash that kept falling), which
is the falling-knife risk.

### The high-CLV side fails

The continuation hypothesis was tested and rejected. In the same harness:

| rule | dev CAGR | dev max DD |
|---|---:|---:|
| CLV > +0.8, hold 2 | **-7.58%** | 84.6% |
| CLV > +0.8, hold 3 | **-1.35%** | 88.7% |
| CLV > +0.6, hold 5 | +27.94% | 87.8% |

A close at the session high is not a continuation signal for QQQ/TQQQ; it is
followed by weak or negative returns. The family's edge is entirely on the
low-CLV reversal side. (These high-CLV cells use the same minute-close CLV as
the primary; the earlier true-daily-high/low scan gave the same sign.)

### CLV versus a plain down-day rule

The obvious competing explanation is that CLV < -0.80 is just a down day. In
the same harness with the same 5-session rolling exit:

| rule | events | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | TQQQ exp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| QQQ down day -> TQQQ, h5 | 871 | 38.84% | **81.8%** | 0.83 | 93.8% |
| QQQ 2-day down streak -> TQQQ, h5 | 366 | 35.13% | 57.6% | 0.83 | 55.1% |
| QQQ 3-day return <= -1.5% -> TQQQ, h5 | 349 | 40.15% | 67.5% | 0.89 | 42.6% |
| **CLV < -0.80 -> TQQQ, h5** | **226** | **79.32%** | **65.98%** | **1.37** | **45.8%** |

The CLV rule is not a re-parameterised down-day rule: it doubles the CAGR of
the plain down-day rule at a lower drawdown and much lower exposure. The
location of the close inside the range carries information beyond the sign of
the day.

## 5. Pre-registered 8-cell grid

All at 1 bp, 1-minute marks. The primary is cell 3.

| # | CLV threshold | hold | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | TQQQ exp | fills |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | -0.60 | 5 | 61.27% | 77.7% | 1.11 | 64.0% | 511 |
| 2 | -0.70 | 5 | 78.60% | 72.1% | 1.32 | 55.9% | 511 |
| 3 | **-0.80** | **5** | **79.32%** | **65.98%** | **1.37** | **45.8%** | 501 |
| 4 | -0.90 | 5 | 51.60% | **55.2%** | 1.14 | 31.2% | 401 |
| 5 | -0.80 | 3 | 61.72% | 57.0% | 1.28 | 30.6% | 653 |
| 6 | -0.80 | 4 | 59.57% | 71.6% | 1.19 | 38.6% | 577 |
| 7 | -0.80 | 6 | 60.14% | 74.8% | 1.13 | 52.0% | 419 |
| 8 | -0.80 | 8 | 48.72% | 81.2% | 0.97 | 61.8% | 323 |

**All 8 cells clear the bar.** The plateau is broad in the threshold (all four
thresholds pass) and in the hold (3 through 8 all pass). The point estimates
vary from 48.7% to 79.3%, so the exact cell is still path-dependent, but there
is no single-cell spike. The shallower thresholds have much higher exposure
and drawdown; the deeper threshold (-0.90) has a lower CAGR but the best
drawdown (55.2%).

The h5 spike (79.3% versus 59.6% at h4 and 60.1% at h6) is the main
path-dependence. The neighbours still clear the bar comfortably, so the family
does not rely on the exact 5-session clock, but the point estimate does.

## 6. Subperiods and drawdown anatomy

| period | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | TQQQ exp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 65.17% | 35.4% | 1.60 | 37.6% |
| 2020-2021 | 180.76% | 63.0% | 1.83 | 48.3% |
| 2022-2023 | **35.65%** | 66.0% | 0.80 | 59.9% |
| ex-2020 | **52.03%** | 66.0% | 1.20 | 39.2% |
| ex-2022 | 91.97% | 63.0% | 1.66 | 37.9% |

The 2016-2019 cut is 65.2% and ex-2020 is 52.0%, both above the TQQQ bar. The
weakest cut is 2022-2023 at 35.65%, just below the bar, because the sleeve is
more invested (59.9%) in the 2022 bear than in any other cut. The strategy is
not a 2020-only result.

**Worst drawdowns:**

| peak -> trough | depth | context |
|---|---:|---|
| 2022-04-05 -> 2022-10-13 | **-66.0%** | the 2022 bear; low-CLV events keep firing |
| 2020-02-26 -> 2020-03-23 | -63.0% | the COVID crash; the rebound rescued the year |
| 2021-12-16 -> 2022-02-24 | -45.8% | the start of the 2022 decline |

The maximum drawdown is 2022, not 2020. That is the falling-knife failure
mode: a close at the low in a sustained bear keeps generating events, and the
5-session hold compounds down. 2022 is -49.8% versus TQQQ -79.4%; the strategy
loses less but still loses half its equity.

## 7. Placebo

Two placebos, each 100 full 1-minute backtests:

| | mean CAGR | sd | p95 | max | p(real >= placebo) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| circular shift of the target | 20.1% | 11.6% | 38.1% | 43.7% | **0.00** |
| random event days | 15.5% | 13.6% | 38.5% | 55.2% | **0.00** |

The shift placebo preserves the event count, clustering and exact exposure;
the random-entry placebo draws the same number of event days uniformly and
runs at 44.8% average exposure (almost exactly the real 45.8%). The real
79.32% is above the maximum of both 100-draw sets. The timing is clearly
distinguishable from both placebos.

## 8. Correlation to the nine current winners

| winner | correlation |
|---|---:|
| family-short-reversal | **0.789** |
| relative-value-tqqq | 0.652 |
| family-ml-microstructure | 0.636 |
| family-rebalance-flow | 0.610 |
| family-session-timing | 0.554 |
| vol-scaled-crash-stop | 0.534 |
| fomc-opex-window | 0.460 |
| family-intraday-microstructure-day | 0.450 |
| ratio-froth | 0.425 |
| TQQQ | 0.789 |

The maximum correlation is 0.789, to `family-short-reversal`, just below the
0.85 kill threshold. CLV is a refined dip-buying signal and it shares the
short-reversal beta, but the CLV object adds a large amount of return at lower
exposure. The report discloses the overlap rather than claiming independence. The stored winner curves were truncated at 2023-12-29 before any return was computed; no 2024-2026 value was inspected.

## 9. Causality and implementation

- CLV uses the 1-minute QQQ closes from 09:30 to 15:59 ET. The 15:59 close is
  the decision point; the target fills at the next 09:30 open. No 16:00 print
  is used.
- `high`/`low` are the max/min of the 1-minute closes, not the official daily
  high/low. The correlation with the official daily CLV is 0.997 and the mean
  absolute difference is 0.033.
- Truncating the panel at the **2020-03-12 11:07** cut leaves **409,376**
  prior weights identical: `max_abs_weight_diff = 0.0`.
- No full-sample normalisation, no moving average, no volatility targeting,
  no drawdown/capitulation event, no calendar clock, no opening-range/VWAP, no
  relative strength, no ML.
- Long-only, weights are 0 or 1, sum <= 1, BIL is the flat asset. 2% band;
  501 fills; 1 bp headline plus 5/10 bp.
- The result is deterministic; the only randomness is the placebo, seeded at
  11.

## 10. Kill criteria - verdict

| # | criterion | value | triggered? |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or DD >= 82.29% | 79.32% / 65.98% | no |
| 2 | fewer than 5/8 grid cells pass | 8/8 | no |
| 3 | 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72% | 69.48% | no |
| 4 | shift-placebo p > 0.05 | 0.00 | no |
| 5 | random-entry placebo p > 0.05 | 0.00 | no |
| 6 | ex-2020 CAGR <= 25% | 52.03% | no |
| 7 | correlation to short-reversal > 0.85 | 0.789 | no |
| 8 | < 100 fills or < 30 events | 501 / 226 | no |
| 9 | pre-cut max weight diff > 1e-12 | 0.0 | no |
| 10 | event-forward t <= 1.5 | 4.31 | no |

**Verdict: dev pass, strong.** All ten kill criteria are clear. The primary
clears the TQQQ bar at 1/5/10 bp, all 8 grid cells pass, both placebos reject
at p = 0.00, ex-2020 CAGR is 52.0%, and the event-level t-stat is 4.31. The
caveats are the 66% drawdown, the -49.8% 2022, the 12,900x turnover, and the
0.789 correlation to `family-short-reversal`. This is a high-return,
high-risk, capacity-constrained dip-buying sleeve, not a low-risk alpha.
hypothesis_md:
# Close location value - `family-close-location`

**Window:** 2016-01-04 -> 2023-12-29, development only. The 2024-2026
holdout is never loaded.

**Family:** close location value (CLV) / where the close sits inside the
session range. The primary object is CLV, not the opening range and not VWAP.

---

## 1. Mechanism

CLV measures where the last price sits inside the session's range:

```
CLV[d] = 2 * (close[d] - low[d]) / (high[d] - low[d]) - 1
```

A close at the session low is -1; a close at the session high is +1. The
family hypothesis allows either continuation (close at the high -> next-session
continuation) or reversal (close at the low -> next-session bounce). The
development scan found the **reversal** side: a close pinned at the session
low is followed by a strong TQQQ bounce over the next week, while a close at
the session high is followed by weak or negative forward returns. The primary
therefore buys the low-CLV event and does not trade the high-CLV event.

The economic story is forced selling / inventory imbalance: when the session
closes at its low, the marginal seller has pushed price to the bottom of the
day's range, and the next sessions mean-revert as that flow finishes. TQQQ is
the long instrument because it gives roughly 3x the QQQ bounce; the cost is 3x
the path risk, which is why the sleeve is flat (BIL) most of the time.

## 2. Exact rules

### Estimation window and decision clock

- `high[d]` and `low[d]` are the maximum and minimum of the **1-minute QQQ
  closes** from 09:30 to 15:59 ET; `close[d]` is the 15:59 ET close. The
  overnight gap is not part of the range.
- CLV is computed once per session at the 15:59 close. It is known at that
  moment and is not revised.
- The target is written on the 15:59 bar and fills at the **09:30 open** of the
  next session.
- No volatility estimate, no moving average, no full-sample normalisation.

Using the range of 1-minute closes rather than the official daily high/low
changes the CLV by a mean absolute 0.033 and gives a 0.997 correlation with the
official daily CLV. The 1-minute-close version is used so that the signal is
derived entirely from the research panel.

### Position rule

```
if CLV[d] < -0.80:
    TQQQ 1.0 for the next 5 sessions
else:
    BIL 1.0
```

A new event while holding rolls the 5-session exit forward. The position is 0
or 1; there is no volatility scaling, stop, profit target or trend filter in
the primary.

### Execution

`research/bt.py`, 1-minute marks, next-open fills, 2% band, long-only,
weights >= 0, sum <= 1. Headline cost 1 bp; 5 bp and 10 bp also reported. BIL is
the flat asset.

## 3. Pre-registered 8-cell grid

The grid was fixed before the final run. It varies the CLV threshold at the
primary 5-session hold, and the hold at the primary threshold.

| # | CLV threshold | hold | role |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | -0.60 | 5 | shallow end |
| 2 | -0.70 | 5 | neighbour |
| 3 | **-0.80** | **5** | **primary** |
| 4 | -0.90 | 5 | deep end |
| 5 | -0.80 | 3 | short hold |
| 6 | -0.80 | 4 | short hold |
| 7 | -0.80 | 6 | long hold |
| 8 | -0.80 | 8 | long hold |

## 4. Falsifiers

The family is rejected, or downgraded to marginal, if any of these hold on
dev:

1. Primary 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or max drawdown >= 82.29%.
2. Fewer than 5 of the 8 grid cells clear the same bar.
3. 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72%.
4. Shift-placebo p > 0.05.
5. Random-entry placebo p > 0.05.
6. Ex-2020 CAGR <= 25%.
7. Daily-return correlation to `family-short-reversal` > 0.85 (which would
   mean CLV is only a re-parameterised down-day rule).
8. Fewer than 100 fills or fewer than 30 independent events.
9. Pre-cut max weight difference > 1e-12.
10. The event-forward 5-session return is not significantly positive
    (t <= 1.5).

## 5. Expected failure modes

- **2022 bear:** a close at the low keeps firing in a sustained decline, and
  the 5-session hold compounds down. The maximum drawdown should be in 2022,
  not 2020.
- **2020 crash:** the same mechanism in February-March 2020; the rebound
  rescues the year but the peak-to-trough loss is large.
- **Turnover:** 5-session holds with overlapping events produce ~12,900x
  turnover at 1 bp. The 10 bp case is the cost stress.
- **Short-reversal overlap:** CLV is correlated with down days; the daily
  correlation to `family-short-reversal` should be high (0.7-0.8). The CLV
  object must add something beyond the down-day rule, and the report compares
  them directly.
- **Small event count:** ~200 independent events over eight years; the
  bootstrap and the placebo are the honest significance tests.

## 6. What this is not

- Not opening-range breakout: the opening range is not computed.
- Not VWAP or close-flow: no volume-weighted price and no volume data is used.
- Not a 20/50/100/150/165/200-day moving-average trend gate.
- Not volatility targeting: the position is 0 or 1.
- Not a drawdown / capitulation event: no peak-to-trough state machine.
- Not a calendar clock, relative strength or ML.
- Not `family-short-reversal`: that rule is a QQQ down-streak / 3-day return;
  this one is the location of the close inside the intraday range, and it
  fires on days that are not necessarily down streaks.

## 7. Design provenance

The CLV was computed from the 1-minute closes on the development window only.
A coarse scan tested both directions:

- high CLV (close at the high) -> continuation: the forward returns were
  negative at the 1-3 session horizons (CLV > 0.8, h2: -7.6% dev CAGR;
  h3: -1.4%), so the continuation hypothesis was rejected;
- low CLV (close at the low) -> reversal: the forward returns were positive and
  increased with the hold, with a sweet spot at CLV < -0.80 and h5.

The threshold/hold grid above was then frozen, and the final run was made once.
No 2024-2026 data was loaded at any point. The high-CLV failure is reported as
a finding, not hidden.

"""Close-location value (CLV) - `family-close-location`.

DEVELOPMENT WINDOW ONLY (2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29).  The 2024-2026 holdout is
never loaded.

Primary signal
--------------
    CLV[d] = 2 * (QQQ_close[d] - QQQ_low[d]) / (QQQ_high[d] - QQQ_low[d]) - 1

where high/low are the maximum/minimum of the 1-minute QQQ closes over
09:30-15:59 ET and close is the 15:59 ET close.  A close at the session low is
CLV = -1; a close at the session high is +1.

Rule: when CLV[d] < -0.80 (close in the bottom tenth of the intraday range),
buy TQQQ at the next session's 09:30 open and hold for 5 sessions.  A new
signal while holding rolls the exit forward to 5 sessions from that signal.
Otherwise hold BIL.  Long-only, no leverage beyond 1.0 TQQQ.

The primary object is CLV, not the opening range and not VWAP.

Run:
    $env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\\Users\\27175\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\pylibs"
    $env:BT_THREADS = "1"
    python research/new/family-close-location/strategy.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research"))
import bt  # noqa: E402

DEV_START, DEV_END = "2016-01-04", "2023-12-29"
BARS_PER_YEAR = 252 * 390
WARM = 20                      # data warm-up, not a trend filter
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SLUG = "family-close-location"

# Pre-registered primary.  The 8-cell grid is fixed in HYPOTHESIS.md.
PARAMS = dict(clv_thr=-0.80, hold=5)

WINNERS = [
    "ratio-froth", "vol-scaled-crash-stop", "relative-value-tqqq",
    "fomc-opex-window", "family-session-timing", "family-short-reversal",
    "family-rebalance-flow", "family-intraday-microstructure-day",
    "family-ml-microstructure",
]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# daily features (all known at the 15:59 close)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def daily_features(ts, o, c):
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    nd = len(first)
    qc = c[last, 0]
    qo = o[first, 0]
    # high/low of the 1-minute closes inside each session
    qh = np.array([c[first[d]:last[d] + 1, 0].max() for d in range(nd)])
    ql = np.array([c[first[d]:last[d] + 1, 0].min() for d in range(nd)])
    rng = np.maximum(qh - ql, 1e-12)
    clv = 2.0 * (qc - ql) / rng - 1.0
    r1 = np.r_[np.nan, qc[1:] / qc[:-1] - 1.0]
    return dict(dates=dates, sess_dates=dates[first], first=first, last=last,
                nd=nd, qc=qc, qo=qo, qh=qh, ql=ql, clv=clv, r1=r1,
                tq=c[last, 1], tqo=o[first, 1], bil=c[last, 2])


def signal_mask(f, params):
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    m = f["clv"] < p["clv_thr"]
    m[:WARM] = False
    return m


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# position -> (n,3) weights
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def positions_from_mask(f, mask, params):
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    nd = f["nd"]
    hold = int(p["hold"])
    pos = np.zeros(nd)
    until = -1
    event_days = []
    for d in range(nd):
        if mask[d]:
            event_days.append(d)
            until = max(until, d + hold)   # rolling exit
        if d < until:
            pos[d] = 1.0
    return pos, event_days


def weights_from_pos(ts, f, pos):
    n = len(ts)
    w = np.zeros((n, 3))
    w[:, 2] = 1.0
    prev = 0.0
    for d in range(f["nd"]):
        target = float(pos[d])
        a, b = int(f["first"][d]), int(f["last"][d])
        w[a:b + 1, 1] = prev
        w[a:b + 1, 2] = 1.0 - prev
        w[b, 1] = target
        w[b, 2] = 1.0 - target
        prev = target
    return w


def build_weights(ts, o, c, params=None):
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    f = daily_features(ts, o, c)
    mask = signal_mask(f, p)
    pos, event_days = positions_from_mask(f, mask, p)
    w = weights_from_pos(ts, f, pos)
    runs = episodes(f, pos)
    info = dict(
        params=p,
        signal_days=int(mask.sum()),
        events=int(len(event_days)),
        event_days=[str(f["dates"][f["first"][d]]) for d in event_days],
        open_at_end=bool(pos[-1] > 0),
        tqqq_exposure=float(np.mean(w[:, 1])),
        episodes=len(runs),
        episode_stats=episode_stats(runs),
        event_forward=forward_event_stats(f, event_days, p["hold"]),
    )
    return w, info


def episodes(f, pos):
    """Contiguous active runs -> (entry_day, exit_day, entry_px, exit_px).

    pos[d] is the target written at the close of day d and filled at the
    next open.  A run starting at s therefore enters at tqo[s+1] and exits
    at tqo[e+1].
    """
    runs = []
    d = 0
    nd = f["nd"]
    while d < nd:
        if pos[d] <= 0:
            d += 1
            continue
        s = d
        while d < nd and pos[d] > 0:
            d += 1
        e = d - 1
        en = s + 1
        ex = min(e + 2, nd - 1)
        if en >= nd:
            continue
        runs.append((s, e, float(f["tqo"][en]), float(f["tqo"][ex])))
    return runs


def forward_event_stats(f, event_days, hold):
    rs = []
    nd = f["nd"]
    for d in event_days:
        en = d + 1
        ex = min(d + 1 + int(hold), nd - 1)
        if en >= nd:
            continue
        rs.append(float(f["tqo"][ex] / f["tqo"][en] - 1.0))
    rs = np.asarray(rs, dtype=float)
    if len(rs) < 3:
        return {"n": int(len(rs))}
    t = float(rs.mean() / rs.std(ddof=1) * np.sqrt(len(rs))) if rs.std(ddof=1) > 0 else None
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    boot = rng.choice(rs, (10000, len(rs)), replace=True).mean(axis=1)
    return {
        "n": int(len(rs)),
        "mean": float(rs.mean()),
        "median": float(np.median(rs)),
        "win": float((rs > 0).mean()),
        "t": t,
        "bootstrap_p": float((boot <= 0).mean()),
        "ci95_low": float(np.quantile(boot, 0.025)),
        "ci95_high": float(np.quantile(boot, 0.975)),
        "worst": float(rs.min()),
        "best": float(rs.max()),
    }


def episode_stats(runs):
    rs = np.array([b / a - 1.0 for _, _, a, b in runs if a > 0 and b > 0])
    if len(rs) < 3:
        return {"n": int(len(rs))}
    t = float(rs.mean() / rs.std(ddof=1) * np.sqrt(len(rs))) if rs.std(ddof=1) > 0 else None
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    boot = rng.choice(rs, (10000, len(rs)), replace=True).mean(axis=1)
    return {
        "n": int(len(rs)),
        "mean": float(rs.mean()),
        "median": float(np.median(rs)),
        "win": float((rs > 0).mean()),
        "t": t,
        "bootstrap_p": float((boot <= 0).mean()),
        "ci95_low": float(np.quantile(boot, 0.025)),
        "ci95_high": float(np.quantile(boot, 0.975)),
        "worst": float(rs.min()),
        "best": float(rs.max()),
    }

# evaluation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _slice(f, pos, start, end):
    i = bt.start_index(TS, start)
    j = int(TS.searchsorted(pd.Timestamp(end, tz="America/New_York"), side="right"))
    return i, j


def metrics(pos, slip=1.0, start=DEV_START, end=DEV_END, w=None):
    if w is None:
        w = weights_from_pos(TS, F, pos)
    if start == DEV_START and end == DEV_END:
        r = bt.run(TS, O, C, w, start, band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
        s = bt.stats(r, BARS_PER_YEAR)
        ww = w
    else:
        i, j = _slice(F, pos, start, end)
        r = bt.simulate(TS[i:j], O[i:j], C[i:j], w[i:j], band=0.02,
                        slippage_bps=slip)
        s = bt.stats(r, BARS_PER_YEAR)
        ww = w[i:j]
    return {
        "cagr": s["cagr"], "max_drawdown": s["max_drawdown"],
        "sharpe": s["sharpe"], "sortino": s["sortino"],
        "volatility": s["volatility"], "fills": s["fills"],
        "turnover": s["turnover"], "ending_equity": s["ending_equity"],
        "tqqq_exposure": float(np.mean(ww[:, 1])),
    }


def daily_returns(pos, slip=1.0):
    r = bt.run(TS, O, C, weights_from_pos(TS, F, pos), DEV_START,
               band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
    eq = pd.Series(r["equity"], index=r["ts"])
    return eq.groupby(eq.index.date).last().pct_change().dropna()


def load_winner_returns(slug):
    """Dev-only segment of a stored winner curve.

    The curve JSON runs to 2026.  Every entry after 2023-12-29 is dropped
    before any value is converted or inspected; only the development segment
    is used.
    """
    path = ROOT / "research" / "new" / "curves" / f"{slug}.json"
    d = json.loads(path.read_text())
    dates = pd.to_datetime(d["dates"])
    keep = dates <= pd.Timestamp(DEV_END)
    vals = np.asarray(d["values"], dtype=float)[keep]
    dates = dates[keep]
    return pd.Series(vals, index=dates).pct_change().dropna()


def correlations(pos):
    sr = daily_returns(pos)
    sr.index = pd.to_datetime(sr.index)
    out = {}
    for slug in WINNERS:
        wr = load_winner_returns(slug)
        j = sr.index.intersection(wr.index)
        out[slug] = float(np.corrcoef(sr.loc[j], wr.loc[j])[0, 1])
    tq = pd.Series(F["tq"], index=pd.to_datetime(F["sess_dates"]))
    tr = tq.pct_change().dropna()
    j = sr.index.intersection(tr.index)
    out["TQQQ"] = float(np.corrcoef(sr.loc[j], tr.loc[j])[0, 1])
    return out


def placebo(pos, mask, params, n_draw=100, seed=11):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    real = metrics(pos)["cagr"]
    seg = pos[WARM:].copy()
    shifts, cagrs = [], []
    for _ in range(n_draw):
        sh = int(rng.integers(20, len(seg) - 20))
        q = np.r_[np.zeros(WARM), np.roll(seg, sh)]
        m = metrics(q)
        shifts.append(m["cagr"])
        cagrs.append(m["cagr"])

    # random event days: same count, same hold rule, timing destroyed
    pool = np.arange(WARM, F["nd"] - 1)
    n_ev = int(mask.sum())
    rand_cagrs, rand_exps = [], []
    for _ in range(n_draw):
        pick = rng.choice(pool, n_ev, replace=False)
        mm = np.zeros(F["nd"], dtype=bool)
        mm[pick] = True
        q, _ = positions_from_mask(F, mm, params)
        m = metrics(q)
        rand_cagrs.append(m["cagr"])
        rand_exps.append(m["tqqq_exposure"])

    def summ(v):
        a = np.asarray(v)
        return {"n_draws": int(len(a)), "mean_cagr": float(a.mean()),
                "std_cagr": float(a.std(ddof=1)),
                "p95_cagr": float(np.quantile(a, 0.95)),
                "max_cagr": float(a.max()),
                "p_value": float((a >= real).mean())}

    s = summ(shifts)
    s["note"] = "circular shift of the daily target vector; preserves exposure, event count and clustering."
    r = summ(rand_cagrs)
    r["mean_exposure"] = float(np.mean(rand_exps))
    r["note"] = "same number of event days drawn uniformly; destroys timing and clustering."
    return {"real_cagr": real, "signal_days": n_ev, "shift": s,
            "random_entry": r}


def precut_check():
    cut = bt.start_index(TS, "2020-03-12")
    w_cut, _ = build_weights(TS[:cut], O[:cut], C[:cut])
    w_full = weights_from_pos(TS, F, F["pos"]) if "pos" in F else None
    if w_full is None:
        return {"error": "no full weights"}
    pre = min(len(w_cut), cut)
    return {"cut": "2020-03-12 11:07 America/New_York",
            "bars_compared": int(pre),
            "max_abs_weight_diff": float(np.max(np.abs(
                w_cut[:pre, 1] - w_full[:pre, 1])))}

TS = O = C = F = None


def main():
    global TS, O, C, F
    TS, O, C = bt.panel(("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"), DEV_START, DEV_END, "1min")
    F = daily_features(TS, O, C)

    mask = signal_mask(F, PARAMS)
    pos, event_days = positions_from_mask(F, mask, PARAMS)
    F["pos"] = pos
    w = weights_from_pos(TS, F, pos)
    info = {
        "params": PARAMS,
        "signal_days": int(mask.sum()),
        "events": int(len(event_days)),
        "tqqq_exposure": float(np.mean(w[:, 1])),
        "episodes": len(episodes(F, pos)),
        "episode_stats": episode_stats(episodes(F, pos)),
        "event_forward": forward_event_stats(F, event_days, PARAMS["hold"]),
    }

    out = {
        "agent": SLUG,
        "family": "close location value",
        "idea": "A close pinned at the session low marks forced selling / "
                "inventory imbalance; the next sessions mean-revert. TQQQ is "
                "the long instrument and BIL is the flat asset.",
        "hypothesis": "QQQ closes in the bottom tenth of its intraday range "
                      "are followed by positive next-open TQQQ returns over "
                      "the next five sessions.",
        "universe": ["QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"],
        "window": {"dev": [DEV_START, DEV_END], "holdout": "not loaded"},
        "execution": {
            "engine": "research/bt.py", "marks": "1min",
            "fills": "next open", "band": 0.02,
            "headline_bps": 1.0, "also_bps": [5.0, 10.0],
            "weight_cap": 1.0, "long_only": True,
            "exposure_state": "TQQQ 1.0 while the CLV event is on, BIL 1.0 otherwise",
        },
        "params": PARAMS,
        "info": info,
        "windows": {"dev": {}},
        "benchmarks": {},
        "yearly": {},
        "grid": [],
        "cuts": {},
        "placebo": {},
        "corr_winners": {},
        "corr_tqqq": None,
        "precut": {},
        "kill_criteria": [
            "dev 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or dev max drawdown >= 82.29%",
            "fewer than 5 of the 8 pre-registered grid cells clear the same bar",
            "10 bp CAGR <= 36.72%",
            "shift-placebo p > 0.05",
            "random-entry placebo p > 0.05",
            "ex-2020 CAGR <= 20%",
            "daily-return correlation to family-short-reversal > 0.85",
            "fewer than 100 fills or fewer than 30 independent events",
            "pre-cut max weight difference > 1e-12",
            "event-forward 5-session t <= 1.5 (CLV reversal absent at the event level)",
        ],
        "status": None,
    }

    for slip, lab in ((1.0, "1bp"), (5.0, "5bp"), (10.0, "10bp")):
        out["windows"]["dev"][lab] = metrics(pos, slip, w=w)
        if slip == 1.0:
            r1 = bt.run(TS, O, C, w, DEV_START, band=0.02, slippage_bps=1.0)

    out["benchmarks"]["tqqq"] = bt.benchmark(C[:, 1], TS, BARS_PER_YEAR)
    out["benchmarks"]["qqq"] = bt.benchmark(C[:, 0], TS, BARS_PER_YEAR)
    out["benchmarks"]["tqqq"]["note"] = (
        "1-minute marks; the task bar is 36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82 on daily closes.")

    out["yearly"] = {int(k): v for k, v in
                     bt.yearly(TS, r1["equity"], C[:, 1]).items()}

    cells = [
        ("1 clv -0.60 h5", dict(clv_thr=-0.60, hold=5)),
        ("2 clv -0.70 h5", dict(clv_thr=-0.70, hold=5)),
        ("3 primary clv -0.80 h5", dict(clv_thr=-0.80, hold=5)),
        ("4 clv -0.90 h5", dict(clv_thr=-0.90, hold=5)),
        ("5 clv -0.80 h3", dict(clv_thr=-0.80, hold=3)),
        ("6 clv -0.80 h4", dict(clv_thr=-0.80, hold=4)),
        ("7 clv -0.80 h6", dict(clv_thr=-0.80, hold=6)),
        ("8 clv -0.80 h8", dict(clv_thr=-0.80, hold=8)),
    ]
    for name, pp in cells:
        p = dict(PARAMS); p.update(pp)
        mm = signal_mask(F, p)
        q, _ = positions_from_mask(F, mm, p)
        m = metrics(q)
        out["grid"].append({"name": name, "params": pp, **m})

    for name, a, b in (("2016-2019", "2016-01-04", "2019-12-31"),
                       ("2020-2021", "2020-01-02", "2021-12-31"),
                       ("2022-2023", "2022-01-03", "2023-12-29")):
        out["cuts"][name] = metrics(pos, 1.0, a, b, w)
    for y in (2020, 2022):
        years = pd.Series(pd.to_datetime(list(F["dates"][F["first"]]))).dt.year.to_numpy()
        mm = mask & (years != y)
        q, _ = positions_from_mask(F, mm, PARAMS)
        out["cuts"][f"ex{y}"] = metrics(q)

    out["placebo"] = placebo(pos, mask, PARAMS)
    out["corr_winners"] = correlations(pos)
    out["corr_tqqq"] = out["corr_winners"]["TQQQ"]
    out["precut"] = precut_check()

    dev = out["windows"]["dev"]["1bp"]
    n_grid = sum(1 for g in out["grid"]
                 if g["cagr"] > 0.3672 and g["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229)
    passes = (dev["cagr"] > 0.3672 and dev["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229
              and n_grid >= 5 and out["placebo"]["shift"]["p_value"] <= 0.05)
    out["status"] = ("dev_pass" if passes and out["windows"]["dev"]["10bp"]["cagr"] > 0.3672
                     else "dev_pass_marginal" if passes else "dev_fail")
    out["grid_cells_above_bar"] = int(n_grid)

    (OUT / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, default=float))
    print(json.dumps({
        "status": out["status"],
        "primary": {k: out["windows"]["dev"][k] for k in ("1bp", "5bp", "10bp")},
        "grid_cells_above_bar": n_grid,
        "corr_tqqq": out["corr_tqqq"],
        "corr_range": [min(out["corr_winners"][s] for s in WINNERS),
                       max(out["corr_winners"][s] for s in WINNERS)],
        "placebo": out["placebo"],
        "precut": out["precut"],
    }, indent=2, default=float))
    print("wrote", OUT / "result.json")


if __name__ == "__main__":
